newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RINGGIT OFF HIGHS VS DOLLAR AFTER RUPIAH NEWS.
newsitem.headline: RINGGIT OFF HIGHS VS DOLLAR AFTER RUPIAH NEWS.

text.p: The ringgit gave back most of its early gains against the dollar after news that Bank of Indonesia has scrapped the daily announcements of its conversion and intervention bands, dealers said.
"The ringgit, like other regional currencies, came under selling pressure again after the news filtered into the market," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
The action by the Indonesian central bank is seen as amounting to a managed float of the rupiah.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7650 to a dollar, after hitting an early high of 2.7510.

The ringgit was earlier helped by local newspaper reports quoting Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad as saying that Malaysia may impose a special tax aimed at curbing speculative attacks on the currency, dealers said.

They said comments by Mahathir on Wednesday that Malaysia will reduce imports and review plans for some large projects due to a sharp fall in the ringgit against the dollar had also tempered the dollar's bullish tone.
But the downside risk for the ringgit was still intact, dealers said, expecting dollar/ringgit to trade in the 2.75-2.80 range in the near term.
